topics.topic: Startup behavior when unreferenced value-byte cleanup fails
questions: What happens when an unreferenced value-byte file cannot be removed: does startup fail, or does the kernel start while leaving the file, and if it remains, may it ever be served or reused?
If an unnamed value-byte file cannot be removed, does startup fail, continue while leaving it unavailable, or handle it like an unremovable spool directory?
What happens when an unreferenced value-bytes file cannot be removed at startup?

judgement.why: This asks the same startup-cleanup-failure question as P1, and neither the relevant text nor the later deciding passages have changed.

precedent.topic: How startup handles failure to remove an unreferenced blob
quotes: open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on a lock file inside data_directory, opened without following links and held for the life of the process; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then remove the module's own temporary files left by an interrupted publish and every file of the content-addressed area whose digest no StoredValue and no file fixture record names, and create the database schema, the content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.

run_start_sequence: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Every step is required: the first step that raises — InstallationRejectedError, RefusedError from the instance check, a store refusal, SandboxUnavailableError, StopRequiredError or any other exception — stops the sequence there and propagates unchanged to the caller with the step named in its reason; no later step runs and nothing is retried or skipped.
precedent.why: The later contracts require open_store to stop on its first failure and require any exception from that startup step to stop the entire start sequence.

topics.topic: Whether failed trial-fixture publications count as unreferenced value bytes subject to cleanup
questions: Does “value bytes no record names” include unreferenced file-fixture bytes published by a failed trial-case store call, or are such fixture bytes excluded and therefore retained by “nothing else is”?

How does startup distinguish an unreferenced value-byte file from an unreferenced trial-fixture file, and what happens to a fixture published by a failed trial-case or capture call before its record is committed?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P2 about whether unnamed trial-fixture bytes are included in startup cleanup, and the relevant texts are unchanged.

precedent.topic: Whether startup cleanup includes unreferenced file-fixture blobs
quotes: open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on a lock file inside data_directory, opened without following links and held for the life of the process; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then remove the module's own temporary files left by an interrupted publish and every file of the content-addressed area whose digest no StoredValue and no file fixture record names, and create the database schema, the content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.
precedent.why: The later startup note explicitly removes content-addressed files whose digest is named by neither a StoredValue nor a file-fixture record.

topics.topic: Ordering of unreferenced-value cleanup relative to startup recovery
questions: Does unreferenced-value cleanup run before startup recovery, after it, or both, and therefore are orphan value bytes created by failed startup recovery removed during that same start or only a later start?

topics.topic: Whether unnamed value bytes must be removed at run end or may persist until next startup
questions: May unnamed value bytes left by a failed call remain after their run ends until the next start, or must they be removed when the run ends to preserve K-10?
